extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, corporate communicators, and press-release writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and distributing news-oriented press releases that follow PRSA standards, covering style, structure, accuracy, modern best practices, and distribution timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary sentence structure: mix simple, compound, and complex sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of sentence types to keep prose engaging and readable; avoid monotonous rhythm. This appears under 'Writing Style Recommendations' as a core stylistic expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés and tired phrases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on overused turns of phrase that dilute originality; both the Writing Style Recommendations and the Implicit Quality Rubric call out avoiding clichés as an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use original imagery and descriptive adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek original images and descriptive adjectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer fresh, specific imagery and precise adjectives rather than generic descriptors; listed both as a writing recommendation and as an implicit quality metric ('Original imagery (not clichés)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Write in active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in active voice (clearer, more concise, more colorful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active constructions throughout to improve clarity and impact. The Implicit Quality Rubric also specifies 'Active voice throughout.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite survey/data details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proper name of survey, who conducted it, and release date when citing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including data or survey results, include the survey's official name, the organization that conducted it, and the release date to ensure verifiability and reporter trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard layout requirement — place client/organization logo at the top and centered to establish branding immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information presence and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact Information: Below logo or in upper right; contact info complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full contact details (name, phone, email) and place them either beneath the logo or in the upper-right of the release. The implicit rubric emphasizes 'Contact info complete.'

rubrics_metrics.name: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE" placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate release status prominently in the upper-right corner so recipients know distribution timing constraints at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline placement and formatting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center the headline directly below the contact info area to make the lead message visually prominent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline location
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the first paragraph with the dateline (city, state, date) to orient reporters immediately to time and place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-paragraph structure (overview)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a concise three-paragraph minimum format: lead/nut grah, quote/context, then background/details. The Implicit Quality Rubric also requires 'Three-paragraph minimum structure.'

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph: nut graph and 5Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph: Date line + nut graph (who, what, when, where).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the 5Ws up front in the nut graph. Modern best practice additionally recommends a 35-word opening paragraph that answers the 5Ws (explicit numeric guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35-word opening paragraph guideline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a modern (2025-2026) best practice, aim for an opening paragraph of about 35 words that concisely covers who, what, when, where, why to maximize immediate news value and scannability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second paragraph: quote and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Second paragraph: Quote and additional context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an attributable quote to add human perspective and provide additional context that supports the nut graph. Keep the quote relevant and news-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Why now" sentence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a concise (about 15 words) sentence that explicitly explains the timeliness or urgency of the news (a focused 'why now'). This is listed as a modern best practice for immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third paragraph: background and details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supporting background, necessary details, and context that reporters may use to deepen a story, but avoid long backstories. Keep this paragraph concise and functional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate presence and placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short company/organization boilerplate near the end of the release to provide standardized background information for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-release signifier
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End the release with '###' as the traditional signifier that no additional content follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-check names; confirm spellings; provide accurate job titles; include institutions responsible for and dates of any cited research; cite all sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoroughly verify all factual elements — names, spellings, titles, institutional attributions, and dates — to maintain credibility. The PRSA Writing Standards and the Implicit Quality Rubric emphasize accuracy and full sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' right to edit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for editorial changes; provide clear, factual copy to minimize necessary edits and maintain core messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid backstory or company history
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid backstory or company history; focus on news itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not bury the news in corporate history. Modern best practices advise eliminating unnecessary backstory and keeping the focus on the immediate news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address current trends and topical framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Address current trends (AI, sustainability, social impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, frame the announcement in relation to current broader trends (e.g., AI, sustainability, social impact) to increase relevance and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timing — optimal weekdays/hours
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule distribution during the recommended window (Thursday late morning to early afternoon) to maximize pickup; use this as a guideline rather than an absolute rule depending on audience and news cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timing — major events lead time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For events, plan outreach well in advance (4–6 weeks) and send a reminder roughly one week before to boost attendance and awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed product launches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For product launches, consider embargoing materials 2–3 days ahead to allow reporters time to prepare coverage while controlling the initial news window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press list curation over blast size
rubrics_metrics.description: Press list curation matters more than blast size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize a carefully curated media list targeted to relevant reporters and outlets rather than sending mass blasts; relevance increases pickup rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper format and minimum structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper format (logo, headline placement, etc.) and three-paragraph minimum structure; boilerplate present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard formatting conventions (logo, contact placement, 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE', dateline, headline, three-paragraph body, boilerplate, '###') to meet journalist expectations and improve usability.
